features.description: Canonical surface vocabulary + alias map (LOAD-BEARING — without it, surface awareness may not route to the right standards). Define ONE closed canonical surface vocabulary, and an alias map that folds the four existing, non-matching vocabularies into it: the plan-review lint surface tags, the qa-sufficiency-contract surface classes, the skill applies_to values, and the agent-conventions topics. The concrete alias table (e.g. the dashboard / read-only-UI / web / ux inputs all resolving to one frontend-ui canonical id; command inputs to a command id; backend/api/service/batch to a backend-api id; infra/deploy to an infra-deploy id; security to a security-review id) is fixed in the plan prose + decisions; unknown inputs resolve to an explicit unrouteable marker rather than being dropped.
steps: Define the closed canonical surface id set (fixed in plan.md / decisions)

Build the alias map resolving each of the four source vocabularies (lint tags, qa-sufficiency classes, skill applies_to, agent-conventions topics) to a canonical id, with an explicit unrouteable fallback
Tests: representative aliases from each source vocabulary resolve to the expected canonical id; an unknown input resolves to unrouteable
features.acceptance: A single closed canonical surface vocabulary exists, plus an alias map that resolves each of the four source vocabularies (plan-review lint tags, qa-sufficiency surface classes, skill applies_to values, agent-conventions topics) to a canonical surface id, with an explicit unrouteable fallback for unknown inputs. Verified by unit tests asserting representative aliases from each source vocabulary resolve to the expected canonical surface (including the web/ux and dashboard inputs converging on one frontend-ui id) and that an unknown input resolves to unrouteable.

features.description: Surface derivation over the canonical vocabulary. Build a pure surface-derivation function that returns the canonical surfaces a plan touches, drawn from its declared surface class plus surfaces inferred from its changed/declared file paths, mapping every input through the F001 alias map so the lint / qa-sufficiency / skill / convention vocabularies converge on one canonical set. Reuse the existing plan-review surface tagging as one input rather than inventing a parallel tagger.
steps: Implement the derivation: union of the declared surface class + path-pattern inference, all resolved through the F001 alias map; keep it pure
Reuse the plan-review lint surface tagging as an input source
Tests: declared-only, path-only, both, and none (empty) cases produce the expected canonical surface set
features.acceptance: A pure surface-derivation function returns the canonical surfaces a plan touches, unioned from its declared surface class and its changed/declared paths and resolved through the F001 alias map, reusing the existing plan-review surface tagging. Verified by unit tests over declared-only, path-only, combined, and empty inputs.

features.description: Sufficiency-pack registry + unrouteable-skills inventory. A declarative map from canonical surface to required convention/skill items (id + what-to-prove + reference). Seed ONLY the frontend pack as the concrete worked example, from the shipped standards (docs/dashboard-design-system.md + docs/qa-sufficiency-contract.md); the other canonical surfaces are NAMED, demand-gated stubs (empty item lists). SEPARATELY, because today the skill-applicability matcher silently skips skills whose SKILL.md lacks applies_to, emit an inventory that LISTS any skill with missing/malformed applies_to as 'unrouteable' — so 'all skills considered' is visible, not silently assumed.
steps: Define the registry shape (canonical surface -> [ {id, prove, reference} ]); seed the frontend pack from the shipped standards
Add the other canonical surfaces as named, demand-gated stubs with empty item lists
Emit an inventory that lists skills with missing/malformed applies_to as unrouteable (not silently skipped)
Tests: the frontend pack lists its seeded items + references; stub surfaces return empty packs; a skill with missing/malformed applies_to appears in the unrouteable inventory
features.acceptance: A declarative sufficiency-pack registry maps each canonical surface to its required items (id + what-to-prove + reference); the frontend pack is seeded from the shipped standards, the other surfaces are named demand-gated stubs, and a skills inventory lists any skill with missing/malformed applies_to as 'unrouteable' rather than silently skipping it. Verified by tests over the seeded frontend pack, the empty stub packs, and an unrouteable-skill fixture appearing in the inventory.

features.description: Disposition vocabulary + ledger (with exact storage). Define the four dispositions (applied / not-applicable / deferred / waived) and a per-plan ledger stored in a DEDICATED conventions ledger file in the plan directory (exact path fixed in decisions, kept out of feature records to avoid bloat). The three non-applied dispositions require a non-empty reason. An applied disposition WITHOUT an evidence reference is a WARN in v0 (not silently ok) — escalation to a BLOCK for user-facing / mutation / security surfaces is deferred to v1. Provide a validator: pack + ledger -> per-item status (ok / missing / invalid-reason / applied-without-evidence).
steps: Define the disposition vocabulary + the per-item ledger entry shape (item id, disposition, reason, evidence)
Fix the ledger storage location (a dedicated per-plan conventions ledger file; path recorded in decisions)
Implement the validator: pack + ledger -> per-item status, requiring a reason for the three non-applied dispositions and warning on applied-without-evidence
Tests: fully-disposed-with-evidence is ok; a missing item is flagged missing; a reasonless waiver is invalid; an applied-without-evidence item is a warn
features.acceptance: A closed disposition vocabulary (applied / not-applicable / deferred / waived) + a dedicated per-plan conventions ledger file (path fixed in decisions) exist, with a validator that flags each applicable pack item as disposed-ok, missing, invalid (a reason is required for the three non-applied dispositions), or applied-without-evidence (a v0 warn). Verified by unit tests over fully-disposed-with-evidence, missing-item, reasonless-waiver, and applied-without-evidence ledgers.

features.description: Advisory plan-review disposition check (v0 = warn, never block). For a plan, derive its canonical surfaces (F002), resolve each surface's pack (F003), validate the ledger (F004), and emit an advisory finding when an applicable item is undisposed, invalid, or applied-without-evidence. Wire it alongside the existing plan-review checks / sufficiency-gate pattern, warn-only — record that BLOCK escalation for user-facing / mutation / security surfaces is deferred (demand-gated, needs false-positive data), mirroring 2026-06-05-002 F006.
steps: Implement the check: for each derived canonical surface with a non-empty pack, warn on missing / invalid / applied-without-evidence dispositions
Surface findings through the existing plan-review report path; keep severity = warn only
Ensure demand-gated stub surfaces (empty packs) never warn; record the BLOCK-escalation deferral as a decision
Tests: a frontend-surface plan with no design-system disposition warns; a fully-disposed plan is clean; a non-surface / stub plan is unaffected
features.acceptance: plan-review emits an advisory (warn, never block in v0) when a plan touches a canonical surface whose pack has undisposed / invalid / applied-without-evidence items, honoring the conventions ledger and leaving demand-gated stub surfaces silent. Verified by tests: a frontend-surface plan missing a design-system disposition warns, a fully-disposed plan is clean, and a non-surface plan is unaffected.

features.description: Wire + dogfood on BOTH synthetic and real history. Connect derivation -> pack -> ledger -> advisory check end to end. Dogfood against (a) a synthetic frontend-surface plan with an incomplete ledger AND (b) one REAL historical plan fixture — a dashboard plan that missed the design-system disposition — proving the gate would have warned on a real failure, not only a synthetic one. Bridge the skill-applicability matcher's output into the ledger's expected items so the existing matcher informs accountability (awareness -> accountability) instead of being a dead-end recommendation.
steps: End-to-end wire the four steps; add a synthetic incomplete-ledger fixture + a real historical plan fixture (the design-system-missing dashboard plan)
Dogfood: both fixtures warn (naming the missing items); a completed ledger is clean
Bridge the skill-applicability matcher output into the ledger's expected items
Capture the two dogfood runs (synthetic + historical) as the objective-contract evidence
features.acceptance: The disposition gate runs end to end and demonstrably warns on BOTH a synthetic incomplete frontend-surface plan AND a real historical plan fixture (the design-system-missing dashboard plan), naming the missing items, then goes clean once disposed; the skill-applicability matcher's output feeds the ledger's expected items. Verified by the two dogfood runs (synthetic + historical) captured as evidence and unit tests over the wired path.
